claims.claim: SO links regulated generation/grid infrastructure to rising electricity demand; nuclear baseload and regulated investment can support reliability as large-load demand expands.
Durable value from large-load growth depends on recoverable infrastructure economics and customer-affordability protections; prospective demand is not equivalent to contracted load.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Firm generation and grid assets matter, but interconnection, regulatory recovery and contracted-load conversion are successor bottlenecks.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Baseline regulated demand is resilient while incremental large-load economics remain conditional.

risks.risk: Large-load capex can create affordability/regulatory pressure if cost allocation is inadequate.

causalEdges.mechanism: higher system load requires firm power and network capacity
causalEdges.falsifier: forecast loads fail to contract/energize or regulators materially disallow recovery

causalEdges.mechanism: dispatchable baseload supports reliability for high-load customers
causalEdges.falsifier: reliability contribution is offset by material availability/cost failures

unknowns.unknown: Share of forward large-load growth contractually committed and project-specific allowed-return economics.

claims.claim: Q2 earnings growth materially outpaced nearly flat operating revenue, so earnings momentum alone does not validate durable demand growth.
The load-growth thesis remains plausible but requires contracted-load and recovery evidence before causal confidence rises.

factors.name: confidenceInflation
factors.basis: Issuer load-growth narrative is stronger than contemporaneous revenue growth.

factors.name: capitalIntensity
factors.basis: Incremental generation/grid build requires substantial capital and regulatory recovery.

risks.risk: Load forecasts may arrive late or below plan while capital is committed.
Affordability or regulatory disallowance can weaken returns.

causalEdges.falsifier: firm contracts and energized load consistently match forecasts

contradictions.claim: Historic load-growth narrative versus nearly flat quarterly operating revenue.
contradictions.resolution: Material timing/economics test, not present falsification; regulated earnings and load timing can diverge from quarterly revenue.

unknowns.unknown: Contracted versus prospective large-load mix and project-specific recovery protections.
